headline: Bane scores 24, Magic rally in 4th quarter to beat Celtics 115-105, extend win streak to 4 games
text: BOSTON -- — Desmond Bane had 24 points and eight rebounds to help the Orlando Magic rally in the fourth quarter and earn their fourth consecutive victory, 115-105 over the Boston Celtics on Monday night. Franz Wagner , who entered the night having scored 30 or more points in each of Orlando’s previous four games, had 21 points, nine assists and eight rebounds. Anthony Black finished with 20 points and seven assists. The Magic shot 50% (41 of 82) from the field in the game to earn their first win in Boston since Dec. 18, 2022. It was Boston's first home loss of the season and snapped the team's six-game win streak. Jayson Tatum led the Celtics with 24 points and 12 rebounds, his first double-double since their season-opening loss at Detroit. But he also had five of his team’s 11 turnovers. Paul George added 22 points and Payton Pritchard had 21 points. The Magic, despite playing on three days of rest, struggled with their shot early. But they still managed to cobble together a 50-41 lead at halftime. Playing on the second night of a back-to-back, the Celtics showed some early signs of fatigue. But they found some traction in the third quarter, led by Tatum’s 14 points to outscore Orlando 36-25 in the period and take a 77-75 lead into the fourth. But the Magic recovered and got an alley-oop from Wagner to Wendell Carter Jr ., followed by a jumper by Bane to take a 110-99 edge with 1:33 left. A night after finishing the first quarter with a franchise-high 33-point lead in its blowout win over Dallas, Boston needed a 3-pointer at the buzzer by Pritchard to even make it to 17 points by the end of the first period on Monday. Both teams had trouble scoring in the opening quarter. The Magic went 7 of 21 (33.3%) from the field, while the Celtics made only 6 of 24 (25%) shots. Up next Magic: Host Philadelphia on Wednesday night. Celtics: Visit Denver on Wednesday night. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

headline: Mitchell and Allen power the Cavaliers to a 126-115 win over the Bulls
text: CLEVELAND -- — Donovan Mitchell scored 39 points and Jarrett Allen added 13 points and 14 rebounds as the Cleveland Cavaliers overcame an early deficit and beat the Chicago Bulls 126-115 on Monday night. Cleveland trailed by six points, 31-25, after one period before rebounding in the second. The Cavaliers used a 32-17 scoring edge in the second quarter for a 57-48 advantage at the break. Cleveland maintained its nine-point lead through the third quarter and weathered a fourth quarter comeback try by the Bulls to win for the third time in four games. Tyrese Proctor scored 10 of his 17 points in the first half for Cleveland, which improved to 6-2 at home. Peyton Watson chipped in 14 points, Meleek Thomas added 10 and James Harden finished with nine points and 10 assists. Norman Powell led Chicago with 27 points, and Matas Buzelis scored 23. Jalen Smith posted 17 points and 11 rebounds, while Tre Jones finished with 16 points and Isaac Okoro had 13. The loss halted the Bulls' two-game win streak, which followed an eight-game skid. Chicago fell to 2-6 on the road and 3-10 overall. The Cavaliers were without Evan Mobley , who has a sprained big toe on his right foot. Cleveland says he will be re-evaluated in seven to 10 days. Up next Bulls: At the Brooklyn Nets on Wednesday. Cavaliers: Host the Memphis Grizzlies on Wednesday. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

headline: Cameron Boozer scores 29 and Grizzlies hand the Wizards an 8th straight loss, 136-120
text: WASHINGTON -- — Memphis rookie Cameron Boozer scored a season-high 29 points in a matchup with top draft pick AJ Dybantsa of Washington, and the Grizzlies rallied from 12 points down to hand the Wizards their eighth straight loss, 136-120 on Monday night. Playing without leading scorer Ty Jerome , who has a sore right hip, the Grizzlies trailed 69-57 in the closing seconds of the first half but took control by outscoring the Wizards 42-18 in the third quarter. Boozer, the No. 3 pick in the draft after a standout season at Duke, finished 7 of 13 on 3-pointers, including two 3s during a 10-0 run that tied the game at 73-all. Zach Edey had 23 points and 10 rebounds for the Grizzlies, who have won four of five and improved to 7-0 on the road. Javon Small had 12 points and 12 assists. Dybantsa matched his season high with 21 points. Washington hasn't won since beating Orlando on Nov. 2 to move to 4-3, and the skid has raised questions about the future of coach Brian Keefe. After a multiyear rebuild, the Wizards hoped to contend this season with veterans Anthony Davis and Trae Young playing alongside Dybantsa. Davis led the Wizards with 23 points. Young, held scoreless for the first time in his career in Sunday night’s 147-119 loss to visiting Houston, had 13 points on 3-of-10 shooting and 12 assists. Young had 10 assists by halftime, the first Wizards player to do that since Tyus Jones on March 10, 2024 at Miami. The only other player with 10 assists in a half this season was Atlanta's Jalen Johnson on Oct. 26 against Houston. The Grizzlies, who entered the game fourth in the NBA in offensive rating, shot 55.8% from the field. Up next Grizzlies: At Cleveland on Wednesday night. Wizards: At Toronto on Wednesday night. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

headline: Embiid has season-high 37 and Brown adds 31 as 76ers beat Nets 135-123 without LeBron James
text: NEW YORK -- — Joel Embiid scored a season-high 37 points, Jaylen Brown matched his season best with 31 and the superstars provided the Philadelphia 76ers with more than enough in LeBron James ' absence to beat the Brooklyn Nets 135-123 on Monday night. Brown added 13 rebounds but wasn't in the game for the finish after a collision with Julius Randle in the fourth quarter opened a cut on his head. Brown returned to the game wearing a headband after being treated, but then left again a few minutes later — though coach Nick Nurse said that departure was because Brown was feeling tightness in his hamstring. James sat out on the second half of the 76ers' back-to-back games and Philadelphia improved to 4-0 without him. Tyrese Maxey finished with 24 points and nine assists. Embiid had 24 points by halftime of what appeared would be a blowout. The Nets made it a game in the fourth quarter before the center helped turn them back, scoring six straight Philadelphia points to extend a six-point lead back into double figures and then making a 3-pointer with 51 seconds remaining after Brooklyn had climbed back within four. Julius Randle scored 33 points and Michael Porter Jr . added 25 for the Nets, who fell to 3-10. Second-year guard Nolan Traore matched his career high with 23 points. Embiid sat out the victory Sunday over Indiana in which James passed Jason Kidd to move into No. 3 on the NBA's career assists list. The 76ers didn't officially list Embiid as available Monday until about half an hour before the game, but it was clear he was fine. He had 13 points in the first quarter as Philadelphia took a 33-26 lead. The Sixers made their first three shots in the second, and when they finally missed, Dean Wade dunked the rebound while being fouled for a three-point play and a 46-28 lead. They made nine of their first 11 shots in the period — and scored on the rebound of that second miss as well. The lead reached 63-39 on Maxey's 3-pointer before Philadelphia took a 78-59 lead to halftime. The Nets charged back into the game in the third, cutting it to 105-95 headed to the fourth. Randle's 3-pointer trimmed it to 106-101 early in the period. Up next 76ers: Visit Orlando on Wednesday. Nets: Host Chicago on Wednesday. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

headline: Giannis Antetokounmpo scores 20, Heat roll past Rockets 128-110 for 5th straight win
text: MIAMI -- — Giannis Antetokounmpo scored 20 points and grabbed 13 rebounds, Andrew Wiggins and Klay Thompson each scored 17 and the Miami Heat never trailed on the way to beating the Houston Rockets 128-110 on Monday night for their fifth straight victory. Davion Mitchell had a 16-point, 10-assist night and Bobby Portis Jr. scored 16 points for the Heat, who have gone 8-2 since starting the season 0-4. Miami was without Bam Adebayo for the second half because of right hip tightness. Thompson made five 3-pointers for the Heat, giving him 2,952 for his career and moving him within 21 of Ray Allen (2,973) for third on the all-time 3s list. Antetokounmpo added six assists — and will now face his former team, the Milwaukee Bucks , for the first time on Wednesday. Alperen Sengun scored 23 points for the Rockets, who were on the second night of a back-to-back and saw their four-game winning streak end. Kevin Durant scored 22 for Houston; he's now up to 32,917 points in his career, 83 shy of the 33,000-point milestone. Only four players — LeBron James , Kareem Abdul-Jabbar, Karl Malone and Kobe Bryant — have scored that many. Houston scored a season-high 147 points against Washington on Sunday night. Things went a little differently on Monday. The Rockets started 1 for 9 from the field and scored only two points in the first 5:54 against the Heat, setting the tone for a night where Houston played uphill the whole way. It was Houston's first loss in six games against Eastern Conference teams this season. The top eight teams in the Western Conference, entering Monday, were 22-3 against teams from the East — winning by an average of 13.4 points. None of those teams had lost to an East opponent by more than 11, before Monday. Up next Rockets: Visit Indiana on Wednesday night. Heat: Host Milwaukee on Wednesday night. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

headline: Terrence Shannon Jr. scores career-high 34 points as Timberwolves beat Trail Blazers 106-98
text: MINNEAPOLIS -- — Terrence Shannon Jr . scored 12 of his career-high 34 points in the second quarter as the Minnesota Timberwolves recovered from a slow start to beat the Portland Trail Blazers 106-98 on Monday night in the opener of a two-game set. Rudy Gobert added 18 points and 15 rebounds for Minnesota, which was coming off a home loss to Chicago on Saturday night. Jaden McDaniels had 13 points for the Timberwolves, who got just six points on 2-of-13 shooting from LaMelo Ball after he went 7 for 25 against the Bulls. Deni Avdija scored 27 points to lead Portland, which had won three in a row and has been playing well under coach Micah Nori, a former Minnesota assistant who made his return to Target Center. Donovan Clingan had 10 points, 10 rebounds and five blocks for the Trail Blazers as his size gave Minnesota trouble, particularly early. Minnesota continues to thrive in the absence of star Anthony Edwards and didn’t have backup guard Jaylen Clark on Monday due to a right hamstring strain. Edwards has missed the past 10 games while recovering from arthroscopic knee surgery. Minnesota is 7-3 in those and had won five in a row before Saturday. Shannon keyed a 21-9 run to end the second half for Minnesota, leading to a 59-51 halftime advantage. With Shannon taking control again early in the fourth, the Timberwolves extended their lead to 19 points and Nori emptied his bench with 7:28 left. Shannon added six rebounds and three assists. Avdija’s drives to the basket helped Portland build a 10-point advantage in the first half as 22 of the Blazers’ first 41 points came in the paint. Up next The teams meet again Tuesday night at Target Center. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

headline: Fears' first triple-double leads the Pelicans past the Warriors 115-94
text: NEW ORLEANS -- — Jeremiah Fears had 19 points, 10 assists and 10 rebounds for his first career triple-double, and the New Orleans Pelicans snapped a six-game losing streak with a 115-94 victory over the Golden State Warriors on Monday night. Saddiq Bey , who hit five 3-pointers, scored 23 points and Zion Williamson added 16 for New Orleans, which led 35-11 after one quarter and maintained a lead that grew as large as 31 points in the third quarter. Pelicans center Yves Missi grabbed 14 rebounds in his second game back from a knee injury that sidelined him 11 games. Yaxel Lendeborg scored a game-high 28 points, Brandin Podziemski scored 15 points and Gui Santos added 12 points for the Warriors, who lost their third straight. It was Golden State's second straight loss by more than 20 points, coming on the heels of a 123-85 defeat at San Antonio on Friday night. The Warriors are without Stephen Curry , who is sidelined at least two weeks with a right oblique tear suffered in a 115-108 loss in Houston on Wednesday. Golden State went 11 of 46 (23.9%) from 3-point range and finished shooting 33.3% (28 of 84) overall. The Pelicans made 15 of 40 3s (37.5%), shot 42.3% (41 of 97) overall, and outscored the Warriors 44-32 in the paint. New Orleans also outrebounded Golden State, 57-50. Fears, drafted seventh overall in 2025, secured his triple-double with his 10th rebound late in the third quarter. The crowd erupted when he grabbed it. Pelicans forward Derik Queen , drafted six spots after Fears, hit a career-high-tying four 3-pointers in a reserve role and finished with 17 points in 20 minutes. Jeron Pierre Jr. added 10 points. Up next Warriors: Visit the Dallas Mavericks on Wednesday. Pelicans: Host the Detroit Pistons on Wednesday. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

headline: Devin Booker scores 20 points, Suns beat Nuggets 117-105 for their 1st road win of the season
text: DENVER -- — Devin Booker led seven Phoenix players in doubles figures with 20 points and the Suns beat the Denver Nuggets 117-105 on Monday night for their first road win of the season. The Suns were playing on the second night of a back-to-back and looked hungrier with a 22-11 advantage in second-chance points. Phoenix, the worst rebounding team in the league, also had a 51-35 edge on the boards in improving to 1/3 away from home. The balanced-scoring attack helped the Suns overcome a big night from Nikola Jokic , who finished with 28 points, 15 rebounds and seven assists. Jamal Murray added 28 despite dealing with foul trouble. The game featured 14 ties and 10 lead changes before Phoenix pulled away in the third quarter. The Suns led by as many as 19 in the fourth before Denver cut it to eight with 43 seconds remaining. The Phoenix bench outscored the Nuggets' reserves by a 42-19 margin. Denver finished with 17 turnovers (Jokic had seven). The team now has five games with 15 or more turnovers. It was Denver's first game at Ball Arena since a 128-109 win over Toronto on Nov. 4. The Nuggets did have a quick trip to elevation in Mexico City when they played Indiana as part of a trip in which the team went 3-1. Murray was hounded up and down the court all night by Dillon Brooks & Co. Brooks picked up a technical foul in the third quarter after making a 3-pointer for appearing to motion toward the Nuggets bench. This marked the second matchup between the teams. Denver won 127-120 at Phoenix on Oct. 30 in an NBA Cup group stage game. Murray and Jokic recently became the first pair of teammates to record 1,000 or more assists to each other since tracking started in 1997-98. “That’s a mind-blowing stat,” Nuggets coach David Adelman said. Up next Suns: At Sacramento on Wednesday. Nuggets: Host Boston on Wednesday. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here
